Have you noticed any specific areas of numbness, weakness on one side of your body, or loss of bowel control in addition to urine?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive difficulty walking. I also have Urinary incontinence, Slurred speech, Rigidity in limbs, Mild hand tremor, Orthostatic hypotension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple System Atrophy (MSA).

The combination of parkinsonism (rigidity, tremor), autonomic failure (orthostatic hypotension, incontinence), and cerebellar/brainstem signs (gait ataxia, dysarthria) is classic for MSA. The MRI findings of atrophy in the brainstem, cerebellum, and basal ganglia further support this neurodegenerative diagnosis.
